name: National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (NCRP)
publisher: Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), Ministry of Home Affairs
lag: n/a for intake; public stats irregular
caveats: Complaint-level geography is the district the COMPLAINANT selects, i.e. victim residence - not the place of harm and not an FIR location
Only a fraction of NCRP complaints convert into FIRs, so NCRP counts and NCRB cyber counts are not reconcilable
State/District monitoring dashboards exist but are law-enforcement-only
Complaint counts track awareness campaigns and the 1930 helpline's publicity as much as incidence
evidence: cybercrime.gov.in listed as I4C's official website in the Wikipedia infobox for Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre. MHA-sourced search summaries state the portal launched 30 Aug 2019, was revamped to accept all cybercrime types, and includes National/State/District-level monitoring dashboards. WebFetch of i4c.mha.gov.in returned EGRESS_BLOCKED; the portal itself was not fetched.
how_to_obtain: Public site accepts complaints only. Aggregate extracts via RTI to I4C or via MHA Parliament answers. Do not attempt to access LEA dashboards.
notes: LOCATION SEMANTICS: victim-residence. Complaint volumes rose 4.52 lakh (2021) to 19.18 lakh (2024); 6.59 million complaints 2021 to Jun 2025.

name: Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C) - institutional outputs and Threat Analytics Unit hotspot analyses
publisher: Ministry of Home Affairs
caveats: I4C TAU 'cybercrime hotspot district' lists are OFFENDER geography (Jamtara JH, Nuh/Mewat HR, Bharatpur and Alwar RJ, Deoghar JH) and must never be merged with NCRP victim-side complaint counts
No standing statistical publication; numbers surface via PIB releases and Parliament answers
evidence: Search index returned this URL with title 'Indian Cybercrime Coordination Centre'. WebFetch returned EGRESS_BLOCKED for i4c.mha.gov.in. Wikipedia confirms I4C's seven verticals including the National Cyber Crime Threat Analytics Unit (TAU), scheme approval Oct 2018 (Rs 415.86 cr, later Rs 782 cr), and attached-office status under MHA w.e.f. 1 July 2024.
how_to_obtain: Parliament question or RTI to I4C for the hotspot-district analysis and underlying mule-account district counts.
notes: THE key offender-vs-victim distinction in the whole scope lives here.

name: State/UT-wise Details of Statistics on National Cyber Crime Reporting Portal (NCRP) Related to Cyber Fraud Cases as on 28-02-2025
publisher: I4C / MHA via NIC Open Government Data (OGD) Platform India
caveats: Snapshot 'as on' a date, not a clean time series - repeated snapshots are the only way to build a panel
State-level only; the district field exists upstream in NCRP but is not in this resource
Cyber FRAUD subset, not all cybercrime
Formats and licence are the OGD platform defaults and were NOT confirmed for this specific resource
evidence: Exact resource title returned by the search index with this URL. WebFetch of www.data.gov.in returned EGRESS_BLOCKED and curl returned CONNECT tunnel failed 403, so columns, row count, formats and licence were NOT confirmed.
how_to_obtain: data.gov.in resource page; OGD also offers a documented API with a free API key. State mirrors (up.data.gov.in, karnataka.data.gov.in) sometimes carry resources the main portal's search does not surface.
notes: The most ingestible cybercrime artifact found in this scope. LOCATION SEMANTICS: victim-residence.

name: Citizen Financial Cyber Fraud Reporting and Management System (CFCFRMS) and National Cyber Crime Helpline 1930
publisher: Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre (I4C), MHA
caveats: 'Amount involved' vs 'amount lien-marked' vs 'amount actually recovered' are three different numbers routinely conflated in press coverage
Geography is the victim's declared district / bank account; the mule-account district is held but never published
Connects 85+ banks, payment intermediaries and wallets - coverage of the long tail of fintech is incomplete
evidence: Described in MHA/PIB-sourced search summaries as a module of NCRP connecting 85 banks/payment intermediaries/wallets and served by helpline 1930. Financial-fraud complaints reported as rising from 2.62 lakh (2021) to 24.02 lakh (2025). No URL for CFCFRMS itself was observed in a search index, so none is recorded.
how_to_obtain: Parliament question for state-wise complaints, amount involved and amount lien-marked; this series has been tabled before. Otherwise RTI to I4C.
notes: LOCATION SEMANTICS: victim-residence / victim's bank.

name: CERT-In annual report and cyber security incident statistics
publisher: Indian Computer Emergency Response Team (CERT-In), MeitY
caveats: NO SPATIAL DIMENSION AT ALL - incidents are attributed to organisations, domains and ASNs, not places. Cannot be mapped.
Counts 'incidents handled', which depends on reporting compliance with the 28 Apr 2022 Directions (6-hour reporting mandate), not on incident occurrence
Different universe from NCRP complaints and NCRB cyber cases - no reconciliation is possible
evidence: Wikipedia infobox gives www.cert-in.org.in; article confirms formation 19 Jan 2004 under IT Act s.70B and the 28 April 2022 Directions requiring reporting of cyber incidents within six hours. Only one figure given: 11.5 million cyberattack incidents in India in 2021. Domain was not fetchable this session.
notes: Catalogue for national-trend context only. Never plot.

name: Sanchar Saathi portal and Chakshu fraud-communication reporting module
publisher: Department of Telecommunications, Ministry of Communications
caveats: Geography is the telecom Licensed Service Area (LSA), which is mostly but NOT state-shaped: Delhi, Mumbai and Kolkata are separate metro LSAs and some LSAs span state borders. Any map needs an LSA-to-district crosswalk.
Counts reports and handsets blocked, which measures app adoption, not fraud incidence
Modules named in press (CEIR, TAFCOP, Chakshu) were not confirmed on the Wikipedia article
evidence: Wikipedia gives sancharsaathi.gov.in, web portal launched May 2023 and mobile app Jan 2025, >700,000 lost/stolen devices recovered by Dec 2025, and ~2,000 fraud incidents reported per day via the app. Domain not fetchable this session.
notes: LOCATION SEMANTICS: subscriber's LSA. A genuinely awkward geography.
how_to_obtain: Public portal is a reporting tool only. For aggregate Chakshu report counts and disconnections by LSA/state, file an RTI with the Department of Telecommunications (Security Assurance wing) or use DoT Parliament answers, which have tabled numbers-disconnected figures before.

name: MHA / MoSJE / MWCD Parliament answers (Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha) carrying state-wise crime annexures
publisher: Ministry of Home Affairs and allied ministries
caveats: Availability is a function of which MP asked a question, not of any publication schedule - the series has holes by construction
Answers reuse NCRB numbers but sometimes restate them with different footnotes, creating spurious discrepancies
Annexure table layouts are unstable between answers
evidence: Two exact PDF paths returned by the search index with the title 'GOVERNMENT OF INDIA MINISTRY OF HOME AFFAIRS LOK SABHA'. mha.gov.in was EGRESS_BLOCKED so neither PDF was opened.
how_to_obtain: Crawl the predictable path pattern MHA1/Par2017/pdfs/par<YYYY>-pdfs/<HOUSE><DDMMYYYY>/<qno>.pdf after confirming it holds. Also use the Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha question databases directly.
notes: The de facto publication channel for at least six domains in this dossier. Highest breadth-per-unit-effort target for Phase 2.

name: NCW Statistical Overview of Complaints (nature-wise complaint reports)
publisher: National Commission for Women
caveats: SELF-SELECTED COMPLAINTS to a Delhi-based commission - Delhi's consistent #1 rank reflects proximity and awareness, not incidence
Per-capita normalisation makes this series MORE misleading, not less: it is an access-to-redress indicator
Categories are NCW's own (domestic violence, dowry, bigamy, refusal to register FIR, etc.), not IPC/BNS heads
No FIR is implied - many complaints are forwarded to police and never registered
evidence: Search index returned this URL with the title 'Statistical Overview of Complaints', and the companion intake system with the title 'Complaints Registration and Monitoring System :: National Commission for Women'. ncwapps.nic.in was not fetchable (EGRESS_BLOCKED / curl 403), so the page structure, categories and refresh cadence are unconfirmed.
how_to_obtain: Direct scrape once verified; check robots.txt and ToU first. For district-level breakdown, RTI to NCW.
notes: LOCATION SEMANTICS: complainant's residence. Closest thing to a refreshing crimes-against-women feed.

name: National Commission for Women Annual Report 2023-24
publisher: National Commission for Women
caveats: Same self-selection bias as the complaint statistics page
Annual report tables are not schema-stable between years
2025 press figures (7,698 complaints; Delhi 688, Maharashtra 473, MP 351, Bihar 342, Haryana 306) come from media reporting of NCW data, not from this PDF
evidence: Search index returned this CDN PDF path under the title 'Ncw'. cdn.ncw.gov.in returned EGRESS_BLOCKED, so table names, page count and whether it contains a state-wise table were NOT confirmed. Wikipedia confirms NCW was established 31 Jan 1992 under the National Commission for Women Act, 1990.
notes: LOCATION SEMANTICS: complainant's residence.

name: State/UT-wise Details of Total Number of Complaints Received in National Commission for Women (NCW) from 2018 to 2023
publisher: NCW via NIC Open Government Data (OGD) Platform India
caveats: Six-year snapshot, ends 2023 - not a live series
Same complaint self-selection bias as all NCW data
The related resource on workplace sexual harassment complaints is YEAR-WISE ONLY (2020-2023), with no state dimension
evidence: Both exact resource titles returned by the search index with these URLs, one on the UP state mirror of the OGD platform. data.gov.in and up.data.gov.in were EGRESS_BLOCKED, so columns, formats and licence were not confirmed.
notes: Note the state-mirror pattern: resources appear on up.data.gov.in and karnataka.data.gov.in that the main portal search does not surface. Worth enumerating mirrors in Phase 2.

name: SHe-Box - Sexual Harassment electronic Box
publisher: Ministry of Women and Child Development
caveats: LOCATION SEMANTICS IS THE WORKPLACE, not the victim's residence and not a police station. A district full of offices will dominate regardless of residential safety.
Covers only the organised/registered workplace universe reachable by Internal Committees; the Local Committee route for small and unorganised workplaces is thinly used
No public statistical output was found
evidence: No URL was observed in any search index or Wikipedia infobox this session, so none is recorded. Wikipedia's article on the Sexual Harassment of Women at Workplace Act, 2013 does NOT mention SHe-Box, but confirms the statutory structure it plugs into: an Internal Complaints Committee at every office or branch with 10+ employees, and a Local Complaints Committee constituted by the District Officer in each district and if required at block level, with action required within 60 days.
how_to_obtain: RTI to MWCD for district-wise SHe-Box complaint counts by year and disposal status. The District Officer / Local Committee structure guarantees a district field exists upstream.
notes: Fourth distinct location semantics in this dossier.

name: One Stop Centres (Sakhi) case data / Mission Shakti MIS
publisher: Ministry of Women and Child Development (Mission Shakti - Sambal)
caveats: SERVICE-DELIVERY-POINT GEOGRAPHY. Coverage equals where OSCs exist and function. A district with no working OSC reports zero cases and would render as 'safe' - the most dangerous false-negative pattern in this scope.
Case counts measure centre throughput and staffing, not violence prevalence
Wikipedia has no article for the One Stop Centre Scheme (HTTP 404), so scheme details here are from general knowledge and must be re-verified
evidence: No URL observed and no page fetched. The Wikipedia article 'Mission Shakti' is about the 2019 anti-satellite test, not the women's safety scheme - a naming collision worth knowing about when searching.
how_to_obtain: RTI to MWCD Mission Shakti division for OSC-wise monthly case registers. State WCD departments hold the same MIS and typically answer faster than the centre.
notes: Always render OSC coverage alongside OSC case counts, or the map lies by omission.

name: Women Helpline 181 call and referral data
publisher: Ministry of Women and Child Development / state governments
caveats: Geography is the state call-centre catchment, not the caller's district
Call volume tracks publicity campaigns
Substantial share of calls are informational, not distress - the denominator is unstable
evidence: No URL observed and nothing fetched this session.
how_to_obtain: RTI to MWCD and to state WCD departments for year-wise 181 call volumes by district and call type.

name: NCPCR complaint and tracking systems - e-Baalnidan, POCSO e-Box, Baalswaraj, SAHARA
publisher: National Commission for Protection of Child Rights
caveats: No public statistical output found for any of the four systems
Baalswaraj is a child-record-level tracking system - almost certainly the richest asset here and correspondingly the hardest to obtain
State Commissions (SCPCRs) mirror this at state level with 36 different practices
evidence: Wikipedia gives ncpcr.gov.in and confirms NCPCR was constituted 5 March 2007 under Section 3 of the Commissions for Protection of Child Rights Act, 2005, and names the portals: e-Baalnidan (all child rights complaints other than POCSO), POCSO e-Box, SAHARA (children of CAPF personnel), a J&K/Ladakh portal, and Baalswaraj (real-time monitoring of children in need of care and protection, with COVID, street-children rescue and POCSO case-tracking modules). ncpcr.gov.in was not fetchable this session.
how_to_obtain: RTI to NCPCR for year-wise district-wise complaint counts by category from e-Baalnidan and POCSO e-Box.

name: TrackChild / Khoya-Paya national portal for missing and found children
publisher: Ministry of Women and Child Development / NIC
lag: n/a for portal; years for publication
caveats: Multiple states reportedly failed to supply data (Delhi, Punjab, Nagaland, Jharkhand, Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, J&K, Andhra Pradesh) - these MUST render as 'no data', never as zero
Recovery rates measure data-entry discipline as much as policing: Kerala 95.0% and Uttarakhand 96.4% against seven states reporting zero cases
'Missing' is a stock/flow muddle - reported-in-year and still-untraced-at-year-end are different numbers and are constantly conflated
Public output is state-level aggregates in Parliament answers; the record-level portal is login-gated
evidence: Search index returned the india.gov.in service page titled 'Portal for missing and tracked children' and an OGD resource titled 'Year-wise Cases of Missing Children Reported on the Track Child Portal including Maharashtra during 2019 and 2020'. Reported 2024 figures: 147,175 children tracked, 67.1% recovery, ~36,000 still missing; West Bengal 22,742 and Madhya Pradesh 19,131. None of the domains were fetchable.
how_to_obtain: RTI to the MWCD Child Protection Division for anonymised year-wise counts by missing-district CROSS recovery-district.
notes: UNIQUE VALUE: TrackChild holds TWO geographies per child - the police station of the missing report and the place of recovery. That origin-destination pair is the only trafficking-corridor dataset in Indian public administration. Highest-value chase in the children domain.

name: CHILDLINE 1098 call and intervention data
publisher: Childline India Foundation (NGO-origin; under MHA administrative control since 2021)
geo_coverage: all-India (602+ districts, 144+ railway stations, 11 bus terminals)
caveats: SERIES BREAK: in 2021 CHILDLINE was brought under MHA administrative control and police personnel replaced social workers on the 1098 line. Pre-2021 and post-2021 call volumes are not comparable.
Geography is the contact-centre catchment (Mumbai, Delhi, Kolkata, Bengaluru, Chennai), not the child's location
Call volume tracks awareness, not incidence - ~1 million calls/month of which only a fraction are interventions
evidence: Wikipedia gives childlineindia.org, founding 1996 by Jeroo Billimoria, ~1 million calls/month, 50 lakh calls answered and 3.95 lakh children rescued or assisted Apr 2020 to Mar 2021, presence in 602+ districts, 144+ railway stations and 11 bus terminals, contact centres in five cities, and the 2021 transfer to MHA administrative control with police personnel handling 1098 calls. The site itself was not fetched.
how_to_obtain: Request district-wise intervention data from Childline India Foundation; post-2021, RTI to MHA.

name: POCSO case registrations, pendency and Fast Track Special Court monitoring
publisher: NCRB (crime head) and Department of Justice, Ministry of Law and Justice (FTSC scheme)
caveats: Wikipedia's POCSO article cites NO statistics on registrations, pendency, conviction rates, FTSCs or the POCSO e-Box, so all figures must be sourced from NCRB or DoJ directly
Rising POCSO registrations partly reflect mandatory-reporting compliance and the criminalisation of consensual adolescent relationships, not only rising abuse
IPC-to-BNS transition (1 July 2024) re-codes the companion IPC sections even though POCSO itself is a special law
evidence: Fetched the Wikipedia POCSO article; it contains no case statistics and no mention of the e-Box. No DoJ or FTSC URL was observed in any search index this session, so none is recorded.
how_to_obtain: Department of Justice FTSC scheme monthly progress reports (state and district-wise court counts and disposals); NJDG for court-level pendency; RTI to DoJ if not published.
notes: LOCATION SEMANTICS: offence location, and clean - POCSO is a contact offence so the FIR police station is normally where it happened. Best-semantics dataset in the children domain.

name: Annual Report under Section 21(4) of the Scheduled Castes and the Scheduled Tribes (Prevention of Atrocities) Act, 1989
publisher: Department of Social Justice and Empowerment, Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
caveats: DENOMINATOR TRAP: rates must use SC/ST population, not total population. Using total population understates atrocity rates in low-SC-share districts and is the standard error in press coverage.
Built on NCRB returns, so it inherits the NCRB principal offence rule - an atrocity accompanying a more serious offence disappears into that offence's count
Registration rates vary hugely with the functioning of each state's SC/ST Protection Cell, so cross-state comparison measures institutional capacity as much as atrocity incidence
Massive pendency distorts any conviction-based measure: 147,545 SC cases pending (92.97%) in 2019 rising to 254,475 (96.1%) in 2021
IPC-to-BNS transition affects the companion IPC sections from 1 July 2024
Report years lag the data year, and the PDF layout changes between editions
evidence: Search index returned the landing page titled 'Annual Reports on Prevention Atrocity Act (PoA) | Department of Social Justice and Empowerment' and two PDFs titled 'REPORT U/s 21 (4) OF THE SCHEDULED CASTES AND THE...'. socialjustice.gov.in was EGRESS_BLOCKED so no PDF was opened. Wikipedia confirms Section 21(4) requires annual reports to be laid before each House, Rule 18 requires states to send annual reports to the Union by 31 March, and gives pendency and conviction figures (2.31% convictions of disposed cases in 2002; <30% per PM in 2009; ~2% for rape cases; 194 exclusive special courts across 11 states in 2019 falling to 176 by 2021). PIB-sourced search summary gives 53,372 cases registered under the Act in 2023.
notes: LOCATION SEMANTICS: offence location, and clean. FLAGSHIP OF THIS SCOPE - best combination of fine geography, honest semantics and statutory continuity.

name: Areas identified as atrocity-prone under Section 17(1) of the SC/ST (PoA) Act read with Rule 3(1) of the 1995 Rules
publisher: State governments (Social Welfare / SC-ST Welfare departments and state SC/ST Protection Cells)
caveats: Notified lists are named-place lists (villages, police station areas, blocks) rather than geometry - geocoding will be manual and lossy
Notification is discretionary and political; absence of notification does not mean absence of atrocities
No central compilation is known to exist - this is 28+ separate state exercises
evidence: Wikipedia's article on the Act confirms that 'Section 17(1) and Rule 3(1) authorize identifying atrocity prone areas to implement preventive measures including firearms licensing restrictions and enhanced monitoring'. No list, notification or URL was located this session.
how_to_obtain: RTI to each state's Social Welfare / SC-ST Welfare Department and to the state SC/ST Protection Cell at police HQ, worded: 'the list of areas identified as atrocity-prone under Section 17(1) of the SC/ST (PoA) Act, 1989 read with Rule 3(1) of the 1995 Rules, with notification numbers and dates'. Several states publish these as district collector notifications in the state gazette.
notes: BEST SEED LEAD IN THE DOSSIER - the only sub-district, officially-designated crime geography found anywhere in this scope.

name: Five Years of Caste-Based Atrocity - An Analysis of Crimes Against Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in India
publisher: National Campaign on Dalit Human Rights (NCDHR) / National Dalit Movement for Justice
caveats: Advocacy publication - reanalysis of NCRB data with a stated normative position; use for the definitional critique and as a cross-check, not as an independent count
evidence: Search index returned this PDF with title 'AN ANALYSIS OF CRIMES AGAINST SCHEDULED CASTES AND SCHEDULED TRIBES IN INDIA'. Not fetched (ncdhr.org.in not attempted; other non-gov domains were blocked).
notes: Best civil-society cross-check for the PoA series.

name: Summary Report - Evaluation Study on Functioning of SC/ST Protection Cells
publisher: Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
caveats: Evaluation narrative, not a data series
evidence: Search index returned this PDF path with title 'SUMMARY REPORT Evaluation Study on Functioning of SC/ST'. socialjustice.gov.in was EGRESS_BLOCKED so it was not opened.
notes: Read before trusting any cross-state comparison of PoA registration rates - it documents how unevenly the district-level Protection Cell machinery actually functions.

name: Anti-Human Trafficking Units (AHTUs) - district-level returns
publisher: MHA Anti-Trafficking Cell (CS Division) and state CIDs
caveats: AHTU existence does not imply AHTU functioning - many are notional postings within a district police office
Rescue counts are destination-side, inheriting the trafficking source/destination trap
No public AHTU-wise data product was located
evidence: No AHTU URL or data product was observed in any search index this session; Wikipedia's 'Human trafficking in India' article contains no information about AHTUs or their numbers.
how_to_obtain: RTI to MHA Anti-Trafficking Cell for AHTU-wise annual returns; parallel RTIs to state CID AHTU nodal officers. Parliament answers periodically table AHTU counts by state.
notes: Each AHTU maps to a district, so the latent granularity is district.

name: NCRB Crime in India - Human Trafficking chapter
publisher: National Crime Records Bureau, MHA
caveats: LOCATION TRAP: the FIR is registered where the victim is RESCUED, i.e. the destination. A choropleth of this marks Delhi, Mumbai and Bengaluru as trafficking hotspots and renders the source districts - the actual policy problem - invisible. Render as origin-destination flow or not at all.
Principal offence rule applies
Trafficking is systematically under-registered and frequently charged under other heads (kidnapping, ITPA, bonded labour)
Definitional change with IPC 370/370A and the BNS re-codification
evidence: ncrb.gov.in confirmed as NCRB's official site via the Wikipedia infobox (NCRB established 11 March 1986). The Human Trafficking chapter's existence and structure were NOT confirmed this session - ncrb.gov.in was not fetchable. Wikipedia's Crime in India article confirms state/UT and city-level tables generally, and cites 1,21,351 children missing as of 2021.
notes: Primary responsibility for NCRB sits with the general-police-statistics agent; catalogued here only for the trafficking-specific tables and the location trap.

name: UNODC Global Report on Trafficking in Persons / UNODC South Asia India outputs
publisher: United Nations Office on Drugs and Crime
caveats: Country-level only - no sub-national geography
Uses UN Trafficking Protocol definitions which do not map cleanly onto Indian crime heads
Depends on Indian government submissions, so it inherits Indian under-registration
evidence: WebFetch of www.unodc.org returned EGRESS_BLOCKED. No URL is recorded because none was confirmed. Useful mainly for definitional alignment with international standards.

name: Narcotics Control Bureau Annual Report 2024
publisher: Narcotics Control Bureau, MHA
caveats: NCB's operating geography is ~23-26 zones, not districts - a zone-to-district crosswalk is required and is lossy
Seizure quantities and values are enforcement output, not drug prevalence
Value figures (Rs 25,330 crore in 2024, +55% on 2023) use notional street values that are not methodologically documented
A second URL (.../Upload/UploadFiles/AnnualReport2024.pdf) appeared only in a search engine's PROSE SUMMARY and not in its result index - treat as unconfirmed and do not hard-code
evidence: Search index returned narcoticsindia.nic.in with title 'Narcotics Control Bureau' and this PDF path under title 'Narcoticsindia'. Wikipedia gives www.narcoticsindia.nic.in, establishment 17 March 1986, NDPS Act 1985 and PITNDPS Act 1988 basis, and the zone list (Mumbai, Indore, Kolkata, Delhi, Chennai, Lucknow, Jodhpur, Chandigarh, Jammu, Ahmedabad, Bengaluru, Guwahati, Patna, plus Agartala, Raipur, Visakhapatnam, Gorakhpur, Jalpaiguri, Itanagar, Bhopal, Cochin, Jaipur, Srinagar, and upgraded units at Amritsar, Dehradun, Mandi). Domain was not fetchable.
notes: LOCATION SEMANTICS: interdiction location.

name: State-wise seizure of drugs all over India by all Drug Law Enforcement Agencies (DLEAs), 2024
publisher: Narcotics Control Bureau, MHA
caveats: SEIZURE LOCATION MEASURES INTERDICTION EFFORT, NOT DRUG PREVALENCE. This series tracks border districts, ports, airports and national highways: Punjab's numbers are about the Pakistan border, Gujarat's about the coast. Rendering seizures as 'drug crime in your neighbourhood' is straightforwardly false.
Aggregates many DLEAs (NCB, DRI, Customs, state police, BSF) with different recording practices
Quantities by drug type are not commensurable without a purity or dose-equivalent assumption
evidence: Search index returned this exact PDF path under the title 'State-wise seizure of drugs all over India by all DLEAs ...'. narcoticsindia.nic.in was not fetchable, so table structure and years covered were not confirmed. The /ImportantSeizure/seizure<YYYY>.pdf pattern suggests a per-year series worth enumerating.
notes: LOCATION SEMANTICS: interdiction location.

name: Magnitude of Substance Use in India (national survey on extent and pattern of substance use)
publisher: National Drug Dependence Treatment Centre (NDDTC), AIIMS New Delhi, for the Ministry of Social Justice and Empowerment
caveats: SURVEY PREVALENCE, NOT CRIME - a different universe from every other entry in this dossier. Do not place on the same layer or in the same legend as enforcement counts.
Sample design supports state-level estimates; district estimates are not statistically supportable
One-off 2019 exercise - a repeat has been discussed but was not confirmed
Combines household survey with respondent-driven sampling of dependent users; the two components have different bias profiles
evidence: No URL was observed in a search index this session, so none is recorded. Wikipedia's 'Drug policy of India' and 'Illegal drug trade in India' articles do NOT mention this survey, the NDDTC, or the National Action Plan for Drug Demand Reduction; the former mentions only that the Narco-Coordination Centre (NCORD) under MHA coordinates agencies.
how_to_obtain: MoSJE publications page and NDDTC/AIIMS site; search the exact title 'Magnitude of Substance Use in India 2019'. Request microdata from NDDTC - the sample frame is district-based even though the published report is state-level.
notes: The ONLY prevalence (as opposed to enforcement) source for narcotics in India.

name: RBI bank fraud statistics (Annual Report frauds section; Report on Trend and Progress of Banking in India; Database on Indian Economy)
publisher: Reserve Bank of India
caveats: NO USABLE GEOGRAPHY: frauds are tabulated by BANK GROUP (public sector / private / foreign) and by fraud category, not by place. The branch where a fraud occurred sits in RBI's internal CRILC/Central Fraud Registry and is never published. Do not attempt to map.
DATE-OF-REPORTING vs DATE-OF-OCCURRENCE: headline counts are by year of REPORTING and frauds are often reported years after they occurred, so the series is not a time series of events
'Amount involved' is not 'amount lost'
Only frauds above reporting thresholds are captured
evidence: Wikipedia infobox gives www.rbi.org.in. The Wikipedia article does NOT list RBI's statistical publications or mention bank fraud statistics, so the publication names above are from general knowledge and must be re-verified. rbi.org.in was not fetchable this session.
notes: Catalogue for a national white-collar context panel only.

name: Enforcement Directorate case statistics (ECIRs, searches, attachments, prosecutions under PMLA/FEMA/FEOA)
publisher: Directorate of Enforcement, Department of Revenue, Ministry of Finance
caveats: Geography is the ZONAL OFFICE that registered the ECIR - an artefact of ED's own org chart (5 regional, 16 zonal, 14 sub-zonal offices), not a crime location
Predicate offences occur elsewhere and often in multiple states
Conviction statistics rest on a tiny completed-trial base (31 PMLA trials completed through July 2023) so the 93.54% conviction rate is not a meaningful rate
No standing statistical publication - numbers emerge via Parliament answers and press briefings
evidence: Wikipedia gives enforcementdirectorate.gov.in, establishment 1 May 1956, enforcement of FEMA 1999 / PMLA 2002 / FEOA 2018, the full regional-zonal-subzonal office list, and statistics as of 31 Jan 2023: 5,906 ECIRs registered and 513 persons arrested; through July 2023, 31 PMLA trials completed with 29 convictions. Domain not fetchable this session.
notes: Useless for spatial crime mapping; catalogue for a white-collar layer only.
how_to_obtain: No standing publication. Obtain via Lok Sabha/Rajya Sabha questions to the Ministry of Finance (Department of Revenue), which routinely table ECIR counts, attachments and prosecutions; or RTI to ED headquarters for zone-wise annual case returns.

name: Serious Fraud Investigation Office case statistics
publisher: Serious Fraud Investigation Office, Ministry of Corporate Affairs
caveats: Case geography would be the accused company's REGISTERED OFFICE - frequently a nominee or chartered-accountant address with no relationship to where harm occurred
Very low case volume; investigates only on referral (Registrar of Companies report, company special resolution, public interest, or government request)
Wikipedia provides no case statistics, so all numbers must come from the MCA annual report or Parliament answers
evidence: Wikipedia gives sfio.gov.in, establishment by GoI resolution 2 July 2003, and statutory status under Section 211 of the Companies Act, 2013. No case statistics in the article. Domain not fetchable.
notes: MCA (Ministry of Corporate Affairs) annual report is the likelier statistical home.

name: SEBI enforcement, adjudication and settlement orders, and SEBI Annual Report
publisher: Securities and Exchange Board of India
caveats: No meaningful geography: entity addresses are corporate-filing addresses and SEBI's own structure is HQ Mumbai plus four regional offices, with 16 of 17 local offices closed in June 2023, further centralising any location signal onto Mumbai
Orders are narrative PDFs - entity names, amounts and provisions require NLP extraction
Enforcement volume reflects SEBI's surveillance priorities of the year
evidence: Wikipedia gives sebi.gov.in, non-statutory establishment 12 April 1988 and statutory status 30 January 1992 under the SEBI Act 1992, HQ at Bandra Kurla Complex Mumbai with Northern (Delhi), Eastern (Kolkata), Southern (Chennai) and Western (Ahmedabad) regional offices, and the June 2023 closure of 16 of 17 local offices. Domain not fetchable.
notes: A high-volume, well-structured order corpus - attractive for NLP, worthless for geography.

name: NHRC custodial death intimations and statistics (police custody and judicial custody)
publisher: National Human Rights Commission of India
caveats: POLICE CUSTODY vs JUDICIAL CUSTODY are routinely conflated - the ~18x gap between 155 and 2,739 for 2024 is exactly this distinction, and ~90% of custodial-death complaints concern judicial custody
NHRC counts INTIMATIONS RECEIVED, so a state with better reporting compliance looks worse - this is a compliance indicator as much as an outcome indicator
Published output is state totals only; the facility identifier sits in the case file

The widely cited '24-hour intimation' requirement derives from NHRC's own directions to Chief Secretaries/DGPs from 1993 onwards, not from the Protection of Human Rights Act text - verify the exact instrument before citing it in the product
Accountability is near-absent: only one instance of disciplinary action reported over five years, so any 'outcome' field will be almost entirely null
evidence: Wikipedia gives https://nhrc.nic.in/, constitution 12 October 1993 under the Protection of Human Rights Act 1993, and oversight of 25 State Human Rights Commissions (formed 1994-2019, most recently Telangana 2019). Search index returned a press-release path nhrc.nic.in/media/press-release/70-37. Reported figures from search summaries: >11,650 custodial deaths 2016-2022; 2,739 custodial deaths in 2024 of which 155 in police custody; 140-176 police-custody deaths annually 2021-2026; Apr 2018 to Mar 2023 687 deaths registered with Gujarat 81, Maharashtra 80, MP 50, Bihar 47; 2025-26 Bihar 19 and Rajasthan 18. Domain was EGRESS_BLOCKED.
how_to_obtain: RTI to NHRC for year-wise custodial deaths by district and by custodial facility, with facility names. NHRC has released facility-level detail in response to specific questions before.
notes: FINEST SPATIAL PRECISION IN THIS DOSSIER. A custodial-death intimation names an exact police station or jail - a true point where victim location, offence location and reporting office all coincide, which is unique here. Ideal for a police-accountability layer.

name: State Human Rights Commissions (25) - annual reports and complaint statistics
publisher: State Human Rights Commissions
caveats: 25 separate sites, 25 separate formats, wildly uneven publication discipline
Several commissions are dormant or have long vacancies in chairperson/member posts, producing artificial drops in complaint counts
No URLs recorded - none were observed in a search index this session
evidence: Wikipedia's NHRC article confirms the existence of 25 State Human Rights Commissions with formation dates ranging from 1994 to 2019, most recently Telangana in 2019, and names commissions in Maharashtra (Mumbai), Tamil Nadu (Chennai) and Uttar Pradesh (Lucknow) among others. No individual SHRC site was located or fetched.
how_to_obtain: Enumerate the 25 commissions from the NHRC site, then per-commission scrape or RTI.
notes: Phase 3 work, not Phase 2.

name: Police Complaints Authorities (State and District) - complaint statistics
publisher: State Police Complaints Authorities, pursuant to Prakash Singh v Union of India (2006)
caveats: Establishment and functioning vary enormously by state; many District PCAs exist only on paper
Publication is sporadic to nonexistent - no standing data product was located
Complaints against police are a distinct universe from crime reports and must never share a layer with them
evidence: A Wikipedia list page confirms the two-tier structure - 'State Police Complaints Authority' with 'District Police Complaints Authority' beneath - but gives no legal-basis detail, mandate or data-publication practice. No URL recorded.
how_to_obtain: RTI to each State PCA for year-wise complaints received and disposed, by district and by nature of allegation. Approach the Commonwealth Human Rights Initiative (CHRI) first - it tracks PCA compliance and is the best civil-society aggregator in this space.

name: MHA communal incident statistics (incidents, deaths, injured, by state)
publisher: Ministry of Home Affairs, largely via Parliament answers; compiled by PRS Legislative Research
caveats: NO STANDING PUBLICATION - availability depends on which MP asked a question in a given year, so the series has structural holes
'Communal incident' has no stable statutory definition; classification is a state police judgement call and is politically contested
Incident counts and death counts move independently and are frequently conflated
State-level only; the district detail that would make this mappable is not published
evidence: Wikipedia's 'Communal violence in India' article cites PRS Legislative Research data with a 2005-2017 table of incidents, deaths and injured by year: an average of 130 deaths/year from communal riots 2005-2009, 24 of 35 states/UTs reporting incidents in that period, Maharashtra highest with 700 incidents, Madhya Pradesh highest fatality rate per 100,000, and an India-wide average of 0.01 deaths per 100,000. Government figures cited for 2012 (93 deaths: 48 Muslims, 44 Hindus, 1 police official) and 2013 (107 killed: 66 Muslims, 41 Hindus). prsindia.org was EGRESS_BLOCKED and no MHA URL for this series was observed, so no URL is recorded.
how_to_obtain: Harvest MHA Parliament answers systematically; start from the PRS Legislative Research compilation for 2005-2017.

name: Varshney-Wilkinson dataset on Hindu-Muslim violence in India
publisher: Ashutosh Varshney and Steven Wilkinson (academic)
caveats: PRESS-REPORT-DERIVED: compiled from Times of India reports, so coverage tracks that paper's editions and city bureaus and systematically under-records small-town riots
Ends 1995 - three decades stale, usable as historical context only
Years, unit of observation and archive location are all UNCONFIRMED by this session
evidence: The Wikipedia biography of Ashutosh Varshney confirms his work on ethnic conflict and the book 'Ethnic Conflict and Civic Life: Hindus and Muslims in India' but does NOT name the dataset, its years, its unit of observation or an archive. The dedicated Wikipedia article for the book returned HTTP 404. A GitHub repository search for 'varshney wilkinson riots dataset' returned 0 results. NO URL IS RECORDED because none was observed.
how_to_obtain: Search ICPSR (Inter-university Consortium for Political and Social Research) for 'Varshney-Wilkinson Dataset on Hindu-Muslim Violence in India'; failing that, contact Brown University's Center for Contemporary South Asia directly. For post-1995 successors, evaluate ACLED's India event data (geocoded, event-level, high cadence) - named as a lead only, with no URL, as it could not be checked this session.

name: ZIPNET - Zonal Integrated Police Network (missing persons, unidentified bodies, stolen vehicles)
publisher: Delhi Police (hosting for participating states)
caveats: Coverage is partial and voluntary - participating states only, so absence means nothing
Record-level personal data on missing persons raises serious privacy and DPDP Act considerations before any republication
Domain zipnet.delhipolice.gov.in appeared ONLY in my own connectivity probe list, NOT in any search index, so it is recorded here as a name rather than a confirmed URL
evidence: Nothing was fetched or seen in a search index. Included on the strength of the domain being a known Delhi Police service; the URL is deliberately NOT placed in the urls object because it was not independently observed.
how_to_obtain: Confirm the portal is live, read robots.txt and terms of use, and assess whether records carry police-station identifiers before any harvesting.
notes: IF live and record-level with station identifiers, this is the finest-grained thing in this dossier and would change what the product can promise for the NCR. Verify early in Phase 2.

name: NCRB Crime in India - Missing Persons tables
publisher: National Crime Records Bureau, MHA
caveats: STOCK vs FLOW MUDDLE: 'reported missing in year' and 'still untraced at year end' are different numbers and are constantly conflated in reporting
State and metropolitan-city level only, no district tables for this head
Missing-person registration practice varies by state; some states discourage registration for adults
Third-party mirrors (Dataful, Indiastat) are commercial and may be paywalled - licence for redistribution is unclear
evidence: Wikipedia's Crime in India article states 1,21,351 children were missing as of 2021 data. Search index returned a Dataful dataset titled 'NCRB: Year, State, and Gender Wise Number Of Children ...' and an Indiastat table 'State-wise Number of Missing Children as per Track Ch...'. dataful.in and indiastat.com were both EGRESS_BLOCKED, and ncrb.gov.in was not fetchable.
notes: Commercial mirrors are a pragmatic Phase 2 shortcut if licensing permits - Dataful in particular publishes NCRB series as clean CSVs.

name: Wildlife Crime Control Bureau - enforcement and seizure data
publisher: Wildlife Crime Control Bureau, Ministry of Environment, Forest and Climate Change
caveats: Same interdiction-effort bias as narcotics: geography is the seizure/enforcement location
Irrelevant to neighbourhood safety - belongs only in a separate environmental-crime layer if at all
No regular seizure-statistics publication was confirmed
evidence: Wikipedia gives wccb.gov.in, statutory provisions in force 6 June 2007 under the Wild Life (Protection) Amendment Act 2006 with the bureau operational from 2008, HQ at Trikoot-1, Bhikaji Cama Place, New Delhi, and involvement in the Wildlife Enforcement Monitoring System with United Nations University and Columbia University's Earth Institute. No data products named in the article. Domain not fetchable.
notes: Low priority, catalogued for completeness.

name: FSSAI food sample surveillance and enforcement statistics (samples analysed, non-conforming, prosecutions)
publisher: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India
caveats: ENFORCEMENT-EFFORT GEOGRAPHY: sample-collection location reflects where food safety officers were deployed, not where adulteration occurs
Lab capacity varies enormously by state (22 referral labs, 72 State/UT labs, 112 notified NABL-accredited private labs), so non-conformance rates are partly a lab-capacity artefact
'Non-conforming' includes labelling and misbranding failures, not only unsafe food - conflating them inflates the adulteration story
evidence: Wikipedia gives www.fssai.gov.in, establishment 5 September 2008 under the Food Safety and Standards Act 2006, and the lab network counts above. The article contains no enforcement statistics and cites a survey in which 73% of 12,308 respondents reported little or no confidence in FSSAI and state food regulators. Domain not fetchable.
notes: Low priority; relevant only to a separate consumer-safety layer.

name: Crime and Criminal Tracking Network and Systems (CCTNS) and Interoperable Criminal Justice System (ICJS)
publisher: National Crime Records Bureau, MHA
caveats: The underlying FIR records ARE police-station-identified - this is the system that could in principle power a police.uk-style map, and the only reason it cannot is policy, not technology
Citizen portal services are limited to individual lookups (FIR copy, tenant/servant verification), not bulk statistics
Data quality and completeness vary by state; several states run parallel legacy systems
Any bulk access raises acute privacy, DPDP Act and defamation exposure - FIR-level data names accused persons who have not been convicted
evidence: Wikipedia confirms CCTNS is an NCRB-implemented e-governance project integrating 'more than 14,000 police stations across the country' with a target of ~15,000 police stations plus 5,000 supervisory offices, holding FIR registration, investigation records and charge sheets in a Core Application Software built by Wipro, with a central citizen portal linked to state citizen portals, and that ICJS integrates CCTNS with e-Courts, e-Prisons, Forensics and Prosecution. NCRB's NAFIS fingerprint system held 1.06 crore records as of 31 October 2024. ncrb.gov.in not fetchable.
how_to_obtain: State-level engagement: several state police departments publish their own CCTNS-derived dashboards and are far more approachable than NCRB. Start with states that already publish crime dashboards.
notes: The structural answer to 'why does India not have police.uk' - the data exists at station level in CCTNS and is simply not released. Worth a dedicated policy-engagement track.
